Hi Elena / ThermoTech billing team,

Attaching a draft invoice for the September subscription + professional services run (invoice_20260930-draft.pdf). Before we finalize: can you confirm the VAT ID you want us to use on the final invoice and whether you want the UK subscription lines treated under reverse-charge?

Context: this invoice has two distinct line groups — (1) monthly per-seat SaaS subscription (recurring) and (2) a one-time implementation services line for professional services delivered during Sept. Our tax team asked us to validate ThermoTech’s VAT ID and confirm place-of-supply for each line so we apply VAT or mark reverse-charge appropriately.

What we need from you:
- Confirm the legal entity that should be invoiced (company name and billing address).
- Provide a VAT certificate or registration number for the invoiced entity (PDF is fine).
- Quick guidance: do you consider the implementation services as performed in the UK (so local VAT applies) or as B2B services where reverse-charge applies?

Goal: we’d like to issue the final invoice this week and avoid a payment hold on collections. If reverse-charge is appropriate for subscription lines we’ll remove VAT and add the statutory note; if services are taxable locally we’ll show VAT on that line only.

Thanks — I’ve cc’d Marcus for tax routing.

Best,

Thanks for the certificate and the quick context. A couple of practical notes from tax: 

1) VAT ID validation: I checked the VAT number you sent against our validation tool and it returns a valid UK VAT registration for ThermoTech Solutions Ltd. That satisfies the B2B reverse-charge requirement for the subscription lines.

2) Line-item treatment recommendation:
   - Subscription (recurring SaaS): treat as B2B supply, apply reverse-charge. Show 0% VAT on those lines and add the standard reverse-charge statutory note: "VAT liable to be accounted for by the customer (reverse charge)" and include the buyer VAT ID.
   - Implementation services (one-off professional services performed in the UK): treat as UK taxable supply — show UK VAT at the applicable rate on the services line.

3) Invoice formatting: best practice is to keep a single invoice with split line items and a summary tax block. That keeps accounting simple for collections while making the tax treatment explicit. Example: two subtotal rows (services + subscription), tax line only for services, and a note for the reverse-charge on the subscription subtotal.

4) Collections & GL mapping: collections should route to the standard EU receivables ledger for invoices with UK VAT; for reverse-charge lines we won’t remit tax but will record the appropriate memo entries. Finance will accept payment without further evidence now that VAT ID validated, but keep the certificate on file.

If you’d like, Rishi can review the draft invoice language for the reverse-charge note before finalizing.

Marcus
Director, Revenue Operations
marcus_lin@redwood.com
